source.title: Accelerated optimization in deep learning with a proportional-integral-derivative controller
source.authors: Song Chen; Jia-Xu Liu; Peng-Kai Wang; Chao Xu; Sheng-Ze Cai; Jian Chu

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out classification performance across optimizers using the paper’s own experiments; this is a conceptual test of V4, not a test of random-label memorization or the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports train and test loss and accuracy for classification models trained with several optimizers. Rows below record the table’s test loss and test accuracy results. It does not test random-label fitting, width sweeps, architecture comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples as posed in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The classification experiments directly compare Adam and adaptive heavy-ball with Momentum on held-out loss and accuracy, bearing on V4. These comparisons remain informative although the paper primarily evaluates PIDAO. Methods specifies matched learning rates and momentum coefficients, rather than an optimizer-specific tuning study; the supplementary settings are not supplied here.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors report improved accuracy and convergence for PIDAO-family algorithms on classification and PDE tasks, associate this with stronger exploration and flatter minima, and acknowledge that the accuracy mechanism remains unresolved. Their computational advantage concerns time to a target loss; runtime per epoch is slightly higher.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces and evaluates a new PID-based optimizer family against standard optimizers; it does not reproduce the original studies’ tuning comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model architecture vary across MNIST, Fashion MNIST, and CIFAR-10; the relative optimizer results differ by dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: PIDAO-family classification performance relative to benchmark optimizers, including PIDopt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PID-based optimization can improve classification performance in the tested recipes; these method comparisons alone do not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD penalty.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 5 associates flatter projected MNIST-FNN loss landscapes with smaller train–test differences for PIDAO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flatness in trajectory-derived principal-component projections accompanies improved generalization in these FNN experiments. This does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or ranking comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: PIDAO and adaptive benchmark comparisons on PINN and FNO PDE solvers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects numerical solution error in the tested scientific-learning tasks; these comparisons lack an SGD/Momentum baseline and fall outside V4's specified benchmarks.

record.problems: The paper reports optimizer hyperparameter settings in supplementary information, but does not present the limited-tuning comparison protocol specified in V4. Classification figures show 90% confidence intervals from 8 experiments; Table 2 reports point values without interval bounds.
record.rows_left_out: Train loss and train accuracy from Table 2 and other experiments were not extracted; selected rows cover the reported held-out classification test metrics relevant to V4.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and comparison with natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and the role of local connectivity; the architectures here use different datasets.

Optimizer-specific learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning, broader tuning, switching Adam to SGD, decoupled weight decay as a recovery intervention on classification benchmarks, and language models. The worse-held-out-despite-equal-or-better-training pattern is not demonstrated by Adam versus Momentum in Table 2.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and compensating training recipes.
Dropout interventions, small-data dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, ranking generalization gaps within a convolutional family, and comparison with norm and margin measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 values and model/dataset assignments are correctly transcribed. Figure 4 reports 90% confidence intervals over eight experiments, but supplied text gives no numerical bounds or pairwise significance tests. States for reversed differences describe point estimates. Matched learning rates do not establish the tuning protocol in V4, and these conditional results do not refute its frequency qualifier. Training metrics were explicitly declared left out, so they are not missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Limited-tuning protocol, broader tuning, switching Adam to SGD, decoupled weight decay, and word-level language models are not tested.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring its effect on test accuracy.
